claims.claim: Huck narrates in his own dialect; Twain told the truth about him in Tom Sawyer, mainly
claims.evidence: 'Mark Twain, and he told the truth, mainly.'

claims.claim: Widow Douglas and her sister Miss Watson try to civilize him
claims.evidence: 'The Widow Douglas she took me for her son, and allowed she would sivilize me'; 'Her sister, Miss Watson'

claims.claim: Tom Sawyer's gang comes for him at night
claims.evidence: 'call it Tom Sawyer's Gang'; Tom's signal at Huck's window

claims.claim: Huck is kept by the Widow Douglas until Pap takes him
claims.evidence: pap and the cabin up the river on the Illinois shore
'blooded the axe good'; Tom: 'it was reckoned I was murdered'

claims.claim: Huck escapes down the Mississippi on a raft with Jim
Jim is Miss Watson's slave, running away
claims.evidence: 'Miss Watson would sell him South, sure'

claims.claim: They meet the Duke and the King
claims.evidence: the king and the duke appear in the doggery/raft chapters

claims.claim: Huck sees the King sell Jim
claims.evidence: Huck returns to find the raft gone; the Duke tells him 'That old fool sold him, and never divided with me' — Huck does not witness the sale

claims.claim: Huck decides to free Jim even at cost of damnation
claims.evidence: 'All right, then, I'll go to hell'—and tore it up

claims.claim: Tom Sawyer turns the rescue into an elaborate game at the Phelps farm
claims.evidence: Tom's evasion plans; Tom: 'what he had planned in his head from the start'

claims.claim: Jim is already free by Miss Watson's will
claims.evidence: 'she set him free in her will'
Jim: the dead man in the floating house 'wuz him'

claims.claim: Huck means to light out for the Territory
claims.evidence: 'I got to light out for the Territory ahead of the rest'

claims.claim: Aunt Sally is Mrs. Phelps, Tom's aunt
claims.evidence: 'Mrs. Phelps'; 'Don't say yes'm—say Aunt Sally'; Aunt Polly is Tom's aunt, Sally is Tom's aunt by marriage ('Sid')
